ai.title: Add device chats marker to Cloud history bearer requests
ai.summary: The Cloud history client in `common` now sends a new HTTP header, `x-freebuff-device-chats`, with every bearer-authenticated request. The header constant is exported as `CLOUD_HISTORY_DEVICE_CHATS_HEADER` and is attached via a shared `bearer` helper that both GET and PATCH calls now use. According to the doc comment, older Desktop clients (0.0.192 and prior) do not send this header and therefore only see hosted chats; clients that can open device-execution chats are expected to include it so the server can return device chats in the listing.
ai.evidence: The diff adds a `CLOUD_HISTORY_DEVICE_CHATS_HEADER` constant and a `bearer` helper in `common/src/desktop-cloud/history.ts`, integrating the new header into all authenticated Cloud history requests.
ai.unknowns: The exact server-side logic that gates device chats on this header is in `web/src/server/desktop-cloud/history-api.ts`, which is not part of this diff.

eli5.text: The shared history tool now automatically adds a marker to its requests whenever you are signed in with a session token, telling the server you can see chats that run on your own computer. This marker is already included in every signed-in request today, so the difference between old and new clients is live in the code. If you use a desktop app that can open chats running on your local machine, the list of your chats can now include those device chats when you are signed in; older desktop apps that never sent this marker will still only see chats hosted by the service.
